newsitem.title: INDIA: India promises APEC-level tariffs by 2010.
newsitem.headline: India promises APEC-level tariffs by 2010.

text.p: India, knocking at the door of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum for membership, will cut tariffs to match the level of forum members by 2010, a senior official said on Wednesday.
Some Asian nations in the 18-member APEC, which aims to achieve free trade by 2020, have said India's tariffs are too high to justify entry.
"Our tariffs will match APEC by 2010," A.N. Ram, a senior Foreign Ministry official, told a news conference.

India is currently an observer in an APEC sub-group on energy, and is in the queue to join two other groups, one on trade and investment and another on science and technology, as part of its drive to become a full member.
Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said during a visit to India last December that if India joined APEC it could lead to other nations qualifying and making the group unwieldy.
In 1991, India launched economic reforms and began cutting import tariffs that for decades had formed a high wall of economic protection.

Ram said India's tariffs were comparable to those of some countries in the seven-nation Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN). "We have a good basis to be considered for (ASEAN) membership," Ram said.
India is not a member of ASEAN, but has the status of a full dialogue partner.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Burma, Laos and Cambodia are to join this year.
